text:
taylor: quick review — noticed a few small but important UX and a11y gaps across roles matrix + invite drawer after yesterday's deploy. jotting them here so we can batch fixes.
shiv: cool, list em.
taylor: 1) roles density — compact mode squeezes chips too tight. Keyboard focus outline overlaps adjacent chips on dark theme. 2) invite drawer: when we toggle the per-invite SSO switch the audit breadcrumb emits a live update and steals focus. 3) copy: inline helper under SSO toggle is missing; tooltip alone isn't discoverable for screen reader users. 4) audit log nav: when a rule change occurs it auto-scrolls and moves focus.
lee: repro'd the focus steal. steps: open org > members > open invite drawer > toggle SSO quickly > press tab. focus lands on breadcrumb link.
nora: for roles density i saw overlapping focus ring in Windows High Contrast and macOS dark. suggestion: increase chip padding by 2px and add 2px accessible outline in forced-colors mode.
shiv: agree on outline. also we should prefer an inset focus ring for chips rather than border to avoid layout shift. add prefers-contrast query to bump contrast.
taylor: for focus trap — root cause is audit breadcrumb re-render setting autofocus when it receives updates. remove programmatic focus on nav updates; instead use aria-live="polite" for the crumb text only.
lee: small code snippet suggestion:
```
// avoid focusing on update
breadcrumb.setAttribute('aria-live','polite')
breadcrumb.removeAttribute('autofocus')
```
and re-evaluate focus-lock after SSO toggle: focusLock.update();
nora: copy idea for SSO helper: short text: "Require company SSO for invited users. Learn more." link to docs. aria-describedby should point from toggle to helper. Example: toggle.setAttribute('aria-describedby','sso-helper');
shiv: also consider placement: per-invite toggle inside drawer (discoverable during invite) + org-level default in settings page with a small banner that says "Default: Require SSO for new users". That avoids surprising overrides.
taylor: audit log nav: when rules change, don't auto-scroll the page. Instead provide a subtle toast in top-right with a link "View audit" that does not take keyboard focus automatically.
ora: accessibility checklist from QA: 1) tab order unchanged after remove role action; 2) removed role chips should be immediately removed from tab sequence (set tabindex=-1 before removal); 3) aria-live region for success/error with role=status; 4) respects prefers-reduced-motion; 5) high-contrast focus visible.
lee: on the removed-chip flow, we should move keyboard focus to the next logical control: next chip, invite button, or role selector. fallback order in code: nextChip || inviteButton || roleSelector || drawerClose.
ora: will add keyboard regression tests: Puppeteer script that tabs through invite drawer after rapid toggles and ensures focus never lands outside drawer.
shiv: design micro-ask: taylor, can you provide exact chip padding and ring color in Figma? also sample text for helper.
taylor: yes — chip padding left/right +4px, top/bottom +2px. focus ring: #FFD166 on dark, 2px inset. helper text: "Require SSO for new users. Learn more." will send Figma slice.
qa-bot: created ticket: INV-4892 "Invite drawer: focus retention and roles chip accessibility" assigned to @nora and @shiv.
taylor: thanks everyone. plan: small copy PR and CSS fix this sprint, JS focus-lock update and e2e next. ping me on the PR for a quick sign-off. :thumbsup:
